local_checks.invariant: No failure path leaves a request pending forever with a live writer, delivers a reply to the wrong request, or reuses a dead child
local_checks.result: An already-aborted signal rejects before spawning (gateway-client.mjs:80-84). Abort fails every pending request, then kills the child (:91-94, :219-224). Round 3 makes #kill forget the child before sending SIGTERM (:226-233): #forget clears the child, ready promise and gate (:235-240), so a request arriving before the old child's close event spawns a fresh child (:131) instead of being written to the dying one. Every #kill call (the ready timer :143-147, abort :91-94, protocol failure :214-217) runs after a #fail that has already rejected the pending requests and the open gate, which clears the ready timer (:155-158). The old child's error, close and stdout handlers are guarded on identity (:161, :167, :178), so once it is forgotten its late events reject nothing that belongs to the new child. A request settles once (:85-90) and removes its abort listener. close() ends stdin and waits for close (:121-128). The adapter registers it as the cordis effect's cleanup (index.mjs:78). Round-3 tests drive in-process fake children through abort, protocol failure and a reply before the ready line (test/gateway-client.test.mjs:53-86, :142-203). Every effect stays inside the operator's own DSH process.

hardening_notes: Aborting one request kills the shared child and rejects every concurrent request of the same client (gateway-client.mjs:91-94, :219-224); concurrent DSH turns in one process lose their in-flight replies. Same-principal availability only.

close() waits for the child's close event with no deadline (gateway-client.mjs:121-128), and since round 3 it returns at once when the child was killed and forgotten (:226-233), without waiting for that child to exit: a gateway that ignores stdin EOF would hang plugin disposal, and one that ignores SIGTERM outlives it. A bounded wait followed by SIGKILL would close both.

The stderr data handler is the one child handler not guarded on identity (gateway-client.mjs:174-176): after a kill and respawn, the forgotten child's late stderr is appended to the tail that #ensureChild reset for the new child (:134), so the new child's GATEWAY_EXIT message can quote the old child's output. Diagnostic mixing within the operator's own process; a `this.#child === child` guard there, as on stdout (:178), would close it.

local_checks.invariant: User content cannot enter or escape the <dsh-system> block, and a forged block gains no authority a user turn lacks
local_checks.result: foldSystem (translate.mjs:185-190) builds one separate {type: 'text'} block from the collected system text only: options.system (:20) and system-role rows (:24-28); user, assistant and tool rows never contribute (:29-38). It unshifts that block in front of the first user message's own content array, or inserts a user message holding it alone (:188-189), so user text blocks stay separate JSON blocks and cannot end or extend the system block's text. The arrays it mutates are built inside toMessagesBody (append :170-175, userContent :199-206), not DSH's history objects. Since round 2 sends no system field (:49), the block is itself user-turn text: a user or tool-result text that spells <dsh-system>...</dsh-system> carries exactly the provenance the folded block has, user-turn text, and no more. System text that contains </dsh-system> ends the tag early. That moves the rest of the text down to plain user-turn text, never up. The tests pin the shapes, and two round-3 tests pass a user text holding a forged <dsh-system>...</dsh-system> with and without system text and assert it stays the user block it was (test/translate.test.mjs:64-153).

local_checks.invariant: No code makes a deterministic trust decision on the tag
local_checks.result: SYSTEM_BLOCK_TAG is defined at translate.mjs:10 and used only by foldSystem (:186) and the test (test/translate.test.mjs:4, :62, :71, :130, :145). A search for dsh-system and SYSTEM_BLOCK_TAG across the plugin finds no reader; the stub selects replies by path, model and the last message's text (stub-gateway.mjs:23-35), and the client writes the body as one JSON line without inspecting it (gateway-client.mjs:107). The model's interpretation of the tag is the only consumer, and the AI companion's core discipline does not count model persuasion without a deterministic control as a boundary failure.

hardening_notes: The <dsh-system> tag is a model-visible convention, not a trust boundary: since no system field is sent, DSH's own instructions (and any project instruction text DSH folds into its system prompt) reach the model with user-turn provenance under the gateway's preset prompt. If a later reader ever treats a <dsh-system> block as authoritative, it must take the block only from the leading position the adapter writes, and the adapter would then need to escape the tag in user and tool text.
